admission.justification: Realized across explainer_staging.py, explainer_server.py, and kernel/atomic_write.py, proved by task-lock serialization and overlapping descriptor-path tests, preventing active staging directories or in-flight atomic temp files from being deleted mid-render.

applicability: Explainer draft staging, publish-time or standalone staging pruning under a review frame task lock, and concurrent same-process atomic_write_bytes calls through distinct directory descriptors.
conditions: Draft allocation and staging cleanup share the frame scope's re-entrant task lock without nesting another resource lock, and concurrent atomic writes share a process using unique pid-and-uuid temporary basenames.
exclusions: Abandoned temporary files left by dead processes from other PIDs, which remain eligible for cleanup once the writer process is gone.
statement: Reading any earlier draft, creating or reusing the publish staging folder, and recording begin_draft execute under one task lock through stage_and_begin_draft, prune_finished_staging runs under the same re-entrant task lock during publish without nesting another resource lock, and atomic_write keys in-flight temporaries by unique basename so concurrent identical renders finish cleanly without deleting each other's temporary files.
title: Draft staging, pruning, and descriptor-anchored atomic writes never race
